LESSON: MOUNT CARMEL CONTEST

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION
Strand: The Bible
Topic 2.6: Mount Carmel Contest

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Mount Carmel Contest. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: how How was God’s power demonstrated in this story?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. explain what Mount Carmel Contest means in simple pupil language
2. give 3 correct examples of Mount Carmel Contest from Kenya
3. practise Mount Carmel Contest in clear steps
4. apply Mount Carmel Contest in one real-life situation this week

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: MOUNT CARMEL CONTEST
Subject: CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION · Grade: Grade 5
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Mount Carmel Contest helps you succeed in CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

KEY FACTS: MOUNT CARMEL CONTEST
Study Mount Carmel Contest like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Explain what Mount Carmel Contest means in simple pupil language

What this means
In this part you learn to explain what Mount Carmel Contest means in simple pupil language. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: explain what Mount Carmel Contest means in simple pupil language.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Mount Carmel Contest” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can explain what Mount Carmel Contest means in simple pupil language. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Give 3 correct examples of Mount Carmel Contest from Kenya

What this means
In this part you learn to give 3 correct examples of Mount Carmel Contest from Kenya. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: give 3 correct examples of Mount Carmel Contest from Kenya.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Story link: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Mount Carmel Contest in your own words.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can give 3 correct examples of Mount Carmel Contest from Kenya. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Practise Mount Carmel Contest in clear steps

What this means
In this part you learn to practise Mount Carmel Contest in clear steps. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: practise Mount Carmel Contest in clear steps.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Daily habit: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can practise Mount Carmel Contest in clear steps. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 4: Apply Mount Carmel Contest in one real-life situation this week

What this means
In this part you learn to apply Mount Carmel Contest in one real-life situation this week. You will use ideas from at home, at your place of worship, and at school.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply Mount Carmel Contest in one real-life situation this week.
2. Reflect, retell, then practise a good habit using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Value in action: Show how “Mount Carmel Contest” looks when you treat a classmate kindly.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply Mount Carmel Contest in one real-life situation this week. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Mount Carmel Contest is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Show how “Mount Carmel Contest” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: explain what Mount Carmel Contest means in simple pupil language)

Example 2: Retell a short faith/values story connected to Mount Carmel Contest in your own words. (skill: give 3 correct examples of Mount Carmel Contest from Kenya)

Example 3: Choose one good action to practise today because of this lesson. (skill: practise Mount Carmel Contest in clear steps)

Example 4: Show how “Mount Carmel Contest” looks when you treat a classmate kindly. (skill: apply Mount Carmel Contest in one real-life situation this week)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Mount Carmel Contest to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: explain what Mount Carmel Contest means in simple pupil language.
3. Practise this skill: give 3 correct examples of Mount Carmel Contest from Kenya.
4. Practise this skill: practise Mount Carmel Contest in clear steps.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Mount Carmel Contest from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Mount Carmel Contest: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 5 learner study Mount Carmel Contest?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. how How was God’s power demonstrated in this story?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Mount Carmel Contest means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: explain what Mount Carmel Contest means in simple pupil language.
5. Be able to: give 3 correct examples of Mount Carmel Contest from Kenya.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
